Based on the earlier thread about Star Wars: The Force Awakens, I wrote a script that calculates the IMDB ratings of a given movie based only on written reviews. Some very interesting findings here, to say the least.

Basically, if the total rating is different from the review rating, something is not right, because we can assume that on average, people who write a review will rate the movie about the same as people who don't write a review.

Let's first look at some classics from the Top 250:

Movie Total score Review Score Difference
The Shawshank Redemption 9.3 9.24 -0.06
The Godfather 9.2 8.85 -0.35
Pulp Fiction 8.9 8.56 -0.34
Star Wars 8.7 8.72 +0.02
Léon 8.6 8.94 +0.34

The deviation is at most about .4. Now let's look at some recent movies:

Movie Total score Review Score Difference
Star Wars: The Force Awakens 8.8 6.60 -2.20
Mad Max: Fury Road 8.2 6.87 -1.33
Interstellar 8.6 7.24 -1.36
Jurassic World 7.1 6.43 -0.67
James Bond 007 - Skyfall 7.8 6.29 -1.51
Iron Man 3 7.3 6.09 -1.21

Note that the results vary strongly between movies. Some look completely normal, for some the deviation is huge only shortly after release and for some the numbers don't add up even some time later.

Here are two recent movies that don't seem to be affected:

Movie Total score Review Score Difference
Guardians of the Galaxy 8.1 7.68 -0.42
Ex Machina 7.7 7.35 -0.35

I've said for some time that I feel the votes for certain movies must be rigged (IMDB votes can be bought on certain websites) and these numbers confirm it in my opinion. The ratings are inflated shortly after release by fake votes and then slowly fall to what you'd expect after some months/years. I expect this to depend mostly on the involved production companies and distributors, but need to do more research.

Thoughts, corrections, more interesting findings, discussion about the cause of this?

It's also why most movies are about a 7, they are only rated by the people who wanted to watch the movie.
